en:
<CLT=cltSTRONG>One high school girl<CLT=cltNORMAL> started the Tragedy.
The Ultimate Despair, Junko Enoshima...

At least, that's what I remember.
But that's not what this book says.

"<CLT=cltSTRONG>Ultimate Despair<CLT=cltNORMAL>" doesn't just refer
to Junko Enoshima...

It refers to a <CLT=cltSTRONG>group<CLT=cltNORMAL> and the <CLT=cltSTRONG>movement<CLT=cltNORMAL>
that came after.

To put it simply, there's more to
Ultimate Despair than Junko Enoshima.

This is the first time I've heard about this.
Wasn't Junko the Ultimate Despair?

...That's what I recall as well. That label
should only apply to her.

Coincidences sure are scary.
Everyone misremembered the same thing.
Coincidence? Misremembered?

<CLT=cltMIND>No, it's no coincidence.
I know there's a difference in these memories.

And that's not all, there are other
discrepancies I'd like to point out.

Ugh, does it even matter?
I'm bored already.
...Just shut up.
So, let's continue where we left off.

Junko resorted to different tactics to
cover the world with despair.

The killing game between the 78th class of
Hope's Peak Academy, for example.

They were locked up and forced into the killing
game by the Ultimate Despair.
But...boo-hoo...

When I, the one who started it all, died, 
events were set in motion...

And the world began to move
towards restoration.

Then the fight between the Future Foundation
and the Remnants of Despair raged on...

But the worst-case scenario was avoided!
Yay, a happy ending!

<CLT=cltMIND>Not yet. There are more points
that conflict with the history.
<CLT=cltMIND>I'll point those out next.
